[http://www.answers.com/topic/isopropyl- ... cat=health](http://www.answers.com/topic/isopropyl-alcohol?cat=health) 

Chemistry

Unlike ethanol or methanol, isopropanol can be separated from aqueous solutions by adding a salt such as sodium chloride, sodium sulfate, or any of several other inorganic salts.[3] The process is colloquially called salting out, and causes concentrated isopropanol to separate into a distinct layer.

I have tried this with table salt.... it works ...the salt and water falls to the bottom and the isopropanol rises to the top

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** Although 91% can be used as the last bath...it is not as bright as using 99%I don't think this is a true statement.

Dave and John did side-by-side tests, and they found each as bright as the other. I should have done likewise, because I would like to see for myself.

One thing I can say is that on some of my recent DCG's (the ones with the Greek impression) the brightness while in the 91% was very substantial, and this was obvious. Looking back, I should have just tried drying this without the 99%. I know it would have been very bright, but side-by-side tests are needed to be sure. Even if the 99% does produce slightly brighter holograms, this would only be needed on holograms that should be "perfect." At least for the holograms I'm doing at the present time, this is not necessary.

On a sidenote, my current source for 91% is not especially cheap, because it only seems to be available in small sizes in stores around here. And it can be expensive to ship a gallon of liquid if it's bought through a mail-order source. When I bought a gallon of 99% from Abra, they charged me a ton for shipping!
